reviews.text:
About a year ago, when we moved from Beijing to Tokyo, we brought our beloved cat, Pumi, who was 21 years old and had chronic kidney disease.

Because of her advanced age and pre-existing conditions, we were very worried about finding a hospital in Japan where we could safely provide care for her. After researching various options, we learned that this hospital allows owners to accompany their pets during examinations and tests, and that the clinic is very quiet and cat-friendly. We contacted them by email beforehand and brought Pumi's test results and medical records from China with us for our visit.

Dr. Yamamoto is a very calm and kind doctor. He was gentle with Pumi throughout, and we were able to receive treatment in a new place with peace of mind.

Also, although our Japanese is not yet fluent, Dr. Yamamoto always chose simple and easy-to-understand language to carefully explain the test results, treatment plan, and medication. Thanks to this, we were able to continue our visits without anxiety.

Throughout this past year, each examination went very smoothly, and whenever we had small concerns, we could immediately contact them by email, and they always replied promptly and kindly, which was incredibly reassuring.

This past Tuesday, Pumi, at 22 years and 1 month old, passed away. Pumi passed away peacefully in her sleep, without suffering greatly, surrounded by her family.

I believe that the last year or so Pumi spent in Tokyo was a time when she could live a new life with peace of mind, thanks to Dr. Yamamoto and all the hospital staff.

And today, Dr. Yamamoto sent flowers as a tribute for Pumi. I was deeply moved by his warm thoughtfulness. He is a truly compassionate doctor who not only provides medical care but also stays by our side until the very end.

I wholeheartedly recommend this hospital to anyone looking for a hospital that treats cats with kindness and care.

I hope that many more cats who visit this hospital will recover and be able to spend many happy years with their families.

My cat is extremely afraid of dogs, so I switched to this cat-only hospital.
There are several veterinarians there.
It seems there are some veterinarians who like cats too.
There are cat books and other things inside the hospital, which is nice.
They are also happy to give advice on various things.
The other day, I took my 2-year-old for a checkup.
Everyone is invited inside so they can have the checkup together.
My child was very well-behaved.
I'm very grateful.

The explanations were thorough, and they listened carefully to my concerns, so I felt truly at ease leaving my pet in their care.
This was my first visit for a teeth cleaning, but I would definitely like to use their services again in the future.
Thank you very much!

Both of my cats are under the care of the head veterinarian. Although we've moved far away, we've decided this is the hospital we'll always use.

The treatment is appropriate and efficient, and they take great care to minimize stress on the cats.

Thanks to the doctor, both of my cats are healthy.

We will continue to rely on their services in the future.

I previously visited this clinic for a second opinion, but the service was absolutely terrible.

My cat had persistent blood in its urine, and when I got home, the floor was covered in blood.

My regular cat specialist couldn't determine the cause, so I desperately searched for a clinic and went to this one to speak with the head veterinarian.

Normally, they would ask questions like, "What are the symptoms?" and "When did it start?"

But the veterinarian was unfriendly, standing silently and not answering until I asked a question.

The information I received was the kind that made the visit unnecessary.

I was left with the impression of an unhelpful veterinarian, and the visit ended in 5 minutes.

While waiting in the waiting room to pay, a woman who looked like a wealthy lady from Shirokanedai was called in and went into the examination room.

Then, I heard the head veterinarian, who had been incredibly unfriendly, happily chatting and laughing.

It became clear to me that they don't need people who only come for a second opinion and aren't likely to return, because they don't bring in any money.

I was stunned by the stark difference in treatment.

It cost 5,500 yen for 5 minutes.

A typical example of a place that's only interested in making money; well, that's the kind of location it is.

Afterward, I took my cat to my current vet, who isn't a cat specialist, and they quickly diagnosed it as bladder stones.

That was the most rude vet I'd ever encountered.

I'm so glad I didn't entrust my cat to them, even though I had my doubts.

I know it's quite difficult,
but if they could make an appointment and respond in an emergency, I'd give it 5 stars.
My cat has been taken care of here for generations. I feel at ease when I go here because they only specialize in cat care.

My regular vet was closed, so I called urgently and they were able to see my cat. My cat has terminal cancer and was experiencing severe bloody stools and loss of appetite, so I requested hydration and vitamin IV fluids.

My cat hates hospitals, but in front of Dr. Yamamoto, she was very calm and didn't tremble at all while receiving the IV fluids. The administration was very skillful, minimizing stress and discomfort for my cat.

Also, the receptionist kindly came outside in the cold to guide me to the parking lot.

Thank you so much for your compassionate care despite the urgent nature of my visit!

I gave it 4 stars because I wanted the vitamin injection to be combined with the IV drip.

The cat-only aspect is wonderful!

I wouldn't even give it one star.
There's no hospital worse than this.
Misdiagnosis after misdiagnosis.

They can't even make a proper diagnosis, and the fees are high; they just take your money.

They made us come back many times unnecessarily, and we had countless useless ultrasounds and blood tests.

Even so, the diagnosis remained unclear, so we went to another hospital for a second opinion, and they found the cause immediately.

While our cat was being treated here,
she suffered terribly. It was heartbreaking to see our usually energetic cat suffering so much every day, so we consulted with others, and when we went to another hospital, she recovered instantly with just one injection.

I shudder to think what might have happened if we had continued going there; she might have died.

And most of all, I feel so sorry and helpless that we chose this hospital and caused our cat so much suffering and prolonged her illness.

Even the veterinarian at the other hospital was shocked.

They call themselves a "Cat Specialist," so you'd think they'd be knowledgeable about cats, but that's not the case at all. I went to this clinic for over a year, based on reviews, but I suspect the positive reviews were just bought.

Some reviews say the clinic director loves cats so much he's like a reincarnation of a cat, but there's absolutely no such atmosphere. Anyone who meets him once will know whether he truly loves cats or not.

Furthermore, the only equipment available is ultrasound and blood tests. Other nearby veterinarians are far better. (There are many veterinarians with better equipment in Minato Ward.)

The waiting room is spacious, but the examination rooms are cramped, the equipment is basic, and it doesn't seem like they consider the cats' well-being.

They claim the ultrasound is high-quality, but it's simply the easiest and cheapest option to install.

With equipment like this, they can't diagnose diseases and will miss them.

A purely business-oriented veterinarian.

Absolutely terrible.

I doubt they're even veterinarians. Their level of expertise is so low. Since veterinarians deal with animals, lawsuits are rare, so they can probably get away with this level of knowledge and equipment, but if you care deeply about your cat, you absolutely should not go there.

They're incredibly profit-driven, and they're sacrificing the lives of both humans and cats.

It was a complete waste of time and money.

I want to sue them.

I've been using this clinic for about four years now. The clinic is very clean, and the staff at reception and other facilities are very polite.

The doctor is my regular doctor, and I've also seen other doctors in emergencies, but they all have cats and put the cat first, so if the cat refuses to get an injection, they'll put it back in its cage to calm it down, which reduces stress for the cat. (The cat won't get irritated after coming home.) Everyone is very skilled, and the procedures are quick and efficient. The facilities are as state-of-the-art as a miniature university hospital. The director and doctors at Jimuta are so good at giving injections that it's almost like they're real cats. (Thank you, lol) Both are male and female.

I usually give this clinic a five-star rating. The receptionists are very friendly, and the female doctor is considerate of my cat's personality, so I've been going there for about five years.

The other day, I had an emergency and the director examined my cat, but he was unfriendly, low-energy, and didn't seem to understand my cat's personality. He was so timid that he ran around the clinic for the first time (I wish he'd even closed the door).

Maybe because he panicked, he only examined me briefly and tried to leave, so I asked him to disinfect the area.

I also finished work early and used my paid leave to bring my cat in on time for the closing time, but he didn't seem to show any consideration for my cat.

I feel very sad and disappointed.

My cat was even more scared than usual, and I felt so guilty.


I'm shocked, especially since I'd read the director's blog.

I have been taking my cats here for three years and can highly recommend. They have helped tremendously with my old cats and their various ailments and needs. Both veterinarians are very friendly and helpful and I can usually get an appointment with not too much notice.

I used this service for an online second opinion. I don't usually write reviews, but I thought this might be helpful to other pet owners.

First of all, the doctor is very reliable, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to provide an online second opinion.

My trusted primary care doctor suspected FMRD and FIP but couldn't give a definitive diagnosis, so I was anxious about future treatment and what tests to recommend. Being able to consult in depth with a doctor who is a cat expert was a great relief for me as an owner.

When you make an online appointment, you will receive a Zoom meeting URL via email. I sent all previous test results in PDF format to the hospital's email address in advance. Payment instructions will be emailed to you after the Zoom session ends.

I also listed the treatment progress in chronological order in the appointment form, and the doctor had read over these documents and prepared them in advance, so he was able to start the consultation with a clear understanding of the situation.

The doctor clearly explained what could be determined from the facts, and he accurately answered questions about the accuracy of the tests we are considering and whether they would be useful for a definitive diagnosis. He told me that the possibility is low, but he also mentioned cases overseas, so I think he was considering the matter from a broad perspective. I now have a clearer idea of ​​how I should think and act going forward. He was a very intelligent and reliable doctor.

I had been told in advance that a diagnosis cannot be made online, so of course I understood that when I consulted. Still, I'm truly glad I consulted him. At my regular doctor's office, I couldn't ask for detailed advice out of consideration for the patients in the back row, but here I was able to speak calmly.
I think pet owners should also prepare in advance before consulting.
It was a wonderful opportunity to talk to a specialist doctor while in the countryside, without putting any strain on my beloved cat. I would like to consult with him again to update him on my progress. Thank you.

It takes 30 minutes by car from my home, but it's a trustworthy hospital. I'm very satisfied with the examinations and treatments.

For some reason, many animal hospitals don't operate on an appointment system, so the waiting time is unpredictable, which is stressful for cats and a problem in emergencies. However, this hospital operates on an appointment system, and they allocate ample time for each appointment. Furthermore, I can bring my cat with me throughout the examination, and they explain things while showing me images. I also really appreciate the cat-first attitude of the doctor and staff. I'd almost like to move closer!
I talked to Kei Taga, a wonderful veterinarian, very helpful and would recommend for everyone ☺️

I use this clinic for regular checkups for my elderly cat. Because they specialize in cats, the waiting time is short. They also offer consultations on weekends, which is reassuring. The prices are also reasonable.

I'm always grateful for the very thorough examinations I receive. The doctors and nurses are all very kind and considerate. 
The waiting room can get crowded at times, but I think it's relatively relaxing. There are lots of books about cats, so I read them while waiting for my appointment. I learn a lot.

I was impressed by how well the doctors and nurses handled the cats. Everyone was very polite and reassuring. It was clear that the head veterinarian had extensive knowledge and expertise. I would definitely recommend this hospital.

Minimize stress for cats! And cats come first!
I've lived with dogs and cats for 40 years.
I've often gone to veterinary clinics, but Dr. Yamamoto is the No. 1 cat-first doctor. He has extensive experience in cutting-edge treatments and is constantly studying research. So, while he values ​​good old-fashioned treatments, he also incorporates new treatments, so I feel at ease. He has good testing equipment and his testing skills are fast and accurate. Thanks to him, my cat's health is stable, and the fees are reasonable. His blood-drawing skills are also amazing. Fast... Like a godsend. He also responds sincerely to inquiries, making him a cat doctor! I really think so.
The waiting room is also relaxing, like a sofa at home.
Since it specializes in cats, I've been going there since I moved. Since it's cat-only, it should be less stressful for the cats.
I had a health checkup. The doctor was very gentle and answered all my questions carefully. I would like to come back next year.

I took my 20-year-old cat to the vet because she was having an epileptic seizure. They explained everything thoroughly, including the risks of the treatment and medication. As expected of a vet specializing in cats, they were very reliable. Thanks to them, she's now healthy again.
